correctness.rationale: Mixed sets dominate immediately except for at most two vertices; when the two singletons have distinct indices, an observed vertex with a third index can force a missing vertex and then the other is forced. For a one-shore set of size at least two, the opposite shore is observed and each of its vertices sees either r or r−1 of the r omitted vertices. This stalls at r≥3, starts a force at r=2, and succeeds at r≤1. A one-shore singleton succeeds on Cr_3=C_6 but stalls for n≥4, and the empty set fails. Counting the disjoint mixed and one-shore classes gives the polynomial and hence the reported total and minimum layers. A separately written bit-mask replay exhausted all 87,360 subsets for 3≤n≤8, checking classification, coefficients, totals and minimum layers; the proof, not the replay, gives all n.
residual_risks: The finite replay is supplemental and not a formal verification.
